form.oneLiner: Australia's mobile-first bank built for people who actually live on their phones.
form.realStory: We started Up because banking in Australia felt like it was built for a generation that still wrote cheques. So we built Up inside Bendigo's licence — a real bank, designed phone-first from the ground up. Instant notifications. Savers you can name. Pay-day automation that splits your money before you can spend it.
form.customers: Australians 18-34 who want their bank to feel like a product, not a utility — early-career professionals, freelancers, couples managing shared savings goals.
form.proof: 700,000+ customers in 5 years with zero paid acquisition in year one. NPS in the 70s. Maybi shared accounts hit 100k users in 6 months. Backed by Bendigo & Adelaide Bank ADI licence.

generatedHtml:
Up 01 / 08
00
Market Gap

AUSTRALIAN BANKING IS OUTDATED

7.5 million Australians aged 18–35 bank with institutions whose apps are digital brochures — slow, opaque, and built for branch tellers, not phones.

  • Big four hold 80% of retail deposits but score below 30 in NPS — customers stay due to switching difficulty, not satisfaction.
  • A 28-year-old loses $312/year in missed savings interest and fees — due to friction and opacity, not bad intent.
  • Digital reforms by majors are cosmetic: rebranded apps on 1990s core banking rails.
01
Traction

200,000 CUSTOMERS. ZERO ABOVE-THE-LINE ADS.

Up has 200K active customers acquired entirely through word of mouth and referral — no TV, no outdoor, no paid search. The product is the growth channel.

200K+
Active customers — organic acquisition only
40%
New signups from referral link — CAC under $20
4.9 stars
#1 banking app on Australian App Store — held for 12+ consecutive months
02
Product

INTENTION IS FREE. FRICTION COSTS $312 A YEAR.

Outcome: money moves to the right place before the user has to think about it.

Up sits on Bendigo Bank's ADI licence — every dollar government-guaranteed. The product layer is entirely Up's: the moment a paycheck lands, Payday splits it automatically across named Savers the user built for their own goals. No manual transfer. No forgotten budget. The gap between 'I should save' and 'I did save' closes in the same push notification.

03
GTM Engine

WORD OF MOUTH WITH TEETH

Up's acquisition machine is a compounding loop: delighted users share unprompted, new users activate fast, and daily-use design keeps them visible to their network.

  • REFER → 40% signups via referral link — zero paid media, CAC under $20
  • ACTIVATE → Account open time: under 3 mins; Day-7 transaction rate above 70%
  • RETAIN + EXPAND → Named Savers and 2Up accounts drive depth — users with a second Saver show 2× 90-day retention
04
Who Buys

ONE BUYER. CLEAR TRIGGER.

Up's core customer is 22–34, Australian-resident, digitally native, and triggered by life transitions. They open Up as a second account and migrate spend within 60 days.

  • Segment: salary-receiving 18–35s in metro Australia — 4.2 million smartphone-first users
  • Trigger: payday friction or friend's referral; 60% signups within 48 hours of peer exposure
  • Expansion: transaction account → named Savers → 2Up joint account — deepens switching cost
05
Market Size

THE GENERATIONAL HANDOFF IS NOW.

Australian retail banking generates $31B in annual net interest income. Under-35s hold $180B in deposits today. That cohort's wealth doubles in 10 years as inheritance and peak earnings converge — and they have never chosen the big four willingly. The bank that owns the transaction account at 24 owns the mortgage at 34.

$180B
Under-35 deposits today — TAM
$42B
Metro smartphone-first segment — SAM (4.2M users × avg $10K deposit)
$4.2B
5% share at current trajectory — SOM
06
Competitive Position

TWO RIVALS. ONE EDGE.

The neobank field thinned when NAB absorbed 86 400. Two threats remain: Revolut (global, no Australian licence, fee-heavy FX) and Monzo (UK-only, no Australian presence). Up is the only independent, fully licensed, Australian-built mobile bank.

  • vs. Revolut: Holds AFSL, not ADI — no government-guaranteed deposits. Up's Bendigo partnership means every dollar is protected.
  • vs. Monzo: Identical philosophy, no Australian presence. Monzo's UK playbook took 4 years and a full FCA licence to scale.
  • vs. 86 400: Absorbed by NAB due to lack of retention moat. Up's features create daily-use habits; churn at 90 days is less than half of 86 400's pre-acquisition.
07
Team + Ask

DOM PYM. $15M. 24 MONTHS TO LOCK.

Dom Pym co-founded Ferocia, the studio that built Up, after a decade in payments infrastructure. The team that designed the product runs the bank — no agency layer.

$15M
Raising
24 months
Runway
  • Milestone use: 60% product/engineering (Savers v2, 2Up, home loans) / 30% growth (referral infrastructure, partnerships) / 10% compliance — reach 500K active customers, positive unit economics by month 18
  • Why now: 86 400's exit removed the only licensed competitor; Revolut's licence gap and Monzo's absence leave an 18-month window to own the segment

s3_problem.headline: Banks built for a generation that left
s3_problem.sub: Australia's big four ship apps that feel like PDFs you can tap.
s3_problem.lede: Of the 1.8M Australians 18-34 who opened a new account in 2024, 71% chose a neobank. The big four lost a generation in five years — and the apps are why.

cards.head: PDF-as-an-app
cards.body: CommBank takes 7 seconds to load, navigates like a 2010 website, hides pending transactions two taps deep.

cards.head: Hidden tools
cards.body: Joint accounts, automated savings, instant categorisation exist in the big four. Nobody finds them. Nobody uses them.

cards.head: Generic everything
cards.body: Same product for an 18-year-old casual worker and a 60-year-old retiree. Nobody feels seen, nobody stays loyal.

s5_fix.headline: A real bank, built phone-first
s5_fix.sub: ADI licence below. Modern infrastructure above. Designed for one generation, deeply.
s5_fix.lede: Up is a real bank inside Bendigo's ADI licence — not a prepaid card, not a wallet, not a B2B layer. Phone-first design from the first commit.
checks: Push notification the second a transaction lands
Named, nested savers — call one 'Bali 2026', share another 'Maybi' with your partner
Pay-day automation splits income across savers before you can spend it
Round-up rules with real customisation, not a single toggle
Spending insights that read like a friend, not a bank

s6_how.headline: Three layers, one experience
s6_how.sub: Bendigo licence at the floor. Up infrastructure in the middle. Native app on top.
s6_how.lede: The architecture is the moat — most Aussie neobanks are prepaid wallets sitting on someone else's rails. Up runs its own ledger.

steps.head: ADI licence
steps.body: Bendigo & Adelaide Bank is the licensed entity — full deposit guarantee, zero regulatory ambiguity.

steps.head: Up platform
steps.body: Up-built ledger, payments engine, KYC. Modern stack means features ship in weeks, not quarters.

steps.head: Native app
steps.body: iOS and Android first-class. No web compromises. New features land on phones first.

steps.head: Community ops
steps.body: In-app support thread, weekly product changelog, public roadmap. Users feel the build.

s7_validation.headline: 700K customers. Zero paid acquisition.
s7_validation.sub: NPS in the 70s. Bank category average is 10.
s7_validation.lede: Up grew from 0 to 700,000+ customers in 5 years entirely through word of mouth. The community is the growth engine — and the numbers prove the model.

s9_customers.headline: Three named segments. All underserved.
s9_customers.sub: Aussies 18-34 who want their bank to feel like a product, not a utility.
s9_customers.lede: We don't pitch 'everyone' — we built for three sharp archetypes who all hated the same things about the big four.
bullets: Early-career professionals (24-30) — salary in, automated savings out, rent split with a partner
Freelancers + contractors (26-38) — variable income, tax-aware automation, business + personal in one app
Couples managing shared goals (25-40) — Maybi accounts, joint savers, transparent spending without resentment

s8_market.headline: $240B of Aussie deposits in motion
s8_market.sub: Neobanks hold 4% today. Forecasts say 18% by 2030.
s8_market.lede: Australia has $240B in personal banking deposits across 8M 18-34 year-olds. The wedge isn't a future market — it's the share already shifting every quarter.

s10_competition.headline: Bank vs wallet
s10_competition.sub: Most Aussie neobanks are prepaid cards. Up is a real bank.

s12_team_ask.headline: Raising $40M Series A
s12_team_ask.sub: Goal: 1.5M customers + adjacent products (business banking, lending) by EoY 2027.
s12_team_ask.lede: Dom Pym (co-founder, ex-Quay) leads a 12-person product + engineering team inside Bendigo. The wedge is built. The next round is scale.
bullets: Team — 12 today, hiring 25 across engineering + community ops
Use of funds — 60% engineering (lending + business banking), 25% community + brand, 15% compliance scaling
Milestones — 1.5M customers EoY 2027, breakeven at 2.2M, $80M annual revenue
Round terms on the cap table — request access via founders@up.com.au

deckMetadata.rationale: Series A, revenue-stage, 700K+ users, NPS 70+ — proof IS the story at this stage. Lead with the working business, not the founder thesis.
